purpose: Single machine-readable source of truth for claims the estate is allowed to make in public copy. scripts/facts-gate.mjs reads this and fails any build whose PRERENDERED output contradicts it.

status_vocabulary.live: Shipped and observable by a stranger today. Quotable in present tense.
status_vocabulary.devnet: Runs, but only on a test network. Never describable as production or mainnet.
status_vocabulary.planned: Code may exist; nothing is live. Only describable in future/conditional tense.
status_vocabulary.retired: Was live, is not. Only describable in past tense.
status_vocabulary.internal: Real internally, NOT a public claim. Must never appear in public copy as fact.

axis_count.note: NEVER frozen as an integer in this file or in page copy. The board is the only authority; a typed number is the first thing to go stale.

observed.note: Observation only, recorded so the gate can detect drift. If this disagrees with the endpoint, the ENDPOINT wins and this block is stale. Recorded after the ADR-001 sweep wired the 8 financial/domain axes into the signed board data and re-signed the payload.

axis_count.api_self_description: Slot counts live in totals (public_count, axes, measured_axes, unmeasured_axes) and are derived from the axis array, never typed.
axis_count.gspc_family_note: The behavioural family's own size, 14, recorded so the gate can recognise the historical measurement stamp '13 canonical axes · jail' as a breakdown of THAT family rather than a competing claim about the 22-axis board. Not a public count — quote totals.public_count.
axis_count.field_note: TWO fields, deliberately. totals.public_count is the SENTENCE a surface quotes; totals.axes is the INTEGER the gate compares against. They are not interchangeable: public_count is a string, and a numeric comparison against it is a type error waiting to be noticed. Until 2026-08-26 the gate read totals.axes while this file declared public_count as the authority — masked only because both happened to yield 14. Both are now named for what they are.
axis_count.grammar_warning: The two numbers mean different things and BOTH must travel. 22 counts SLOTS on the board; 15 counts slots with a measurement behind them. Claiming the larger number as measured would assert 7 measurements that do not exist. Quote the sentence, or quote the smaller number.

twenty_two_figure.authority: Owner ruling 2026-08-24, csoai-static-deploy2 commit 2bdbac34986333f6de992fcd76cb08aa3e19d1cf; recorded in council-os/ADR-001-axis-count.md. Backed on the wire by GET /api/gspc -> totals.axes == 22 after the sweep of 2026-08-26.
twenty_two_figure.note: '22' is a count of AXES ON THE BOARD — never a count of measurements. 14 GSPC behavioural axes + 8 financial/domain axes. 15 of the 22 carry a measurement; 7 are declared slots published so the gap is visible.
correct_forms: 15 measured axes of 22 on the board
twenty_two_figure.why_it_was_internal_until_now: This block previously read status 'internal', public_claim false, and 'not corroborated by any live surface'. That was ACCURATE at the time and is exactly why the fix had to be a data task: the 8 financial axes were ruled in on 2026-08-24 but absent from the signed board payload, so no live surface could corroborate the number. The two 2026-08-26 00:xx commits that locked the public board at 14 (5477ef62, ebec824e) forbid TYPING 22 without data behind it — a guardrail against inventing the number, not a repeal of the ruling. The sweep wired the axes in and re-signed; the number is now corroborated by the artifact it summarises, which is the condition those guardrails were written for.
twenty_two_figure.standing_caveat: The ruling's own wording applied the word 'measured' to the full slot count. The evidence supports 22 axes and 15 measurements. The evidence wins, and no axis was marked MEASURED to close the gap. The exact phrase is listed under forbidden_forms for the gate to match on, and is deliberately not repeated in prose where a reader could mistake it for a claim.

namespaces.note: Axis counts are per-instrument. A count is only a contradiction WITHIN one namespace. These are distinct instruments and legitimately carry their own counts. A namespace entry lists the surfaces that legitimately render ITS count; the gate exonerates those surfaces from comparison against the board number. An entry with no surfaces listed gets no exoneration — which is the mechanical reason 27 arena-derived counts were flagged against the board until 2026-08-26.

gspc_board.self_description_note: The board is the count authority, so its own payload and signed snapshot are exonerated from being compared against themselves. The payload legitimately describes its own composition; flagging the authority against itself is a tautology, not a check.

gspc_gap_map.observed: 4 axes (G, S, P, C) + care_cost lens

arena_elo.authority: GET /api/arena/scoreboard (axis_pass_rates keys) for the pass-rate view; /arena/elo_reference.json (axes[]) for the signed Elo reference.
arena_elo.observed: 17 axes in the signed Elo reference (12 models); 15 axes in the live pass-rate scoreboard.
arena_elo.distinct_instrument: The arena is NOT a stale copy of the GSPC board and must not be reconciled to the board's number. It measures a different thing over a DIFFERENT SET of axes: its ids include slot15 and human-vs-ai — which the board's own limitations say are measured in-lane and never counted in board totals — plus accountability, creativity, efficiency, fairness, privacy, sovereignty and transparency, which are not board axes at all. Forcing these to one number would destroy information, not fix a contradiction. This matches docs/operations/COUNT_GRAMMAR_2026-08-26.md: precise sets, no forced reconciliation.
arena_elo.internal_gap_flagged_for_owner: The arena's own two surfaces still differ from each other (17 signed reference vs 15 live scoreboard), and the signed reference's axis entries carry empty name fields. That is a real gap WITHIN this namespace, not resolved by the ADR-001 board sweep. Owner decision: name the arena's count authority and re-sign the reference once its axis set is settled.

namespaces.surface_matching: Each entry may carry `surface` (one path) or `surfaces` (a list). An entry ending in '/*' matches by prefix, for a route family such as the 26 /gspc/:axis pages. Trailing '/index' is stripped before matching.

financial_axes_register.authority: /interop/financial-axes.json — the register for the 8 financial/domain axes
financial_axes_register.observed: 8 axes, 1 measured (provenance-controls); 7 declared slots with no run
financial_axes_register.note: These 8 are also carried on the GSPC board, where they count toward the axis count and NOT the measured count. This register is the per-axis detail behind those rows and legitimately states its own family's count of 8.

anchoring.sentence: Nothing Council of AI publishes is anchored to a blockchain — every record is anchored by an Ed25519 signature over a SHA-256 hash chain rooted in did:web:csoai.org; where a ledger appears, we are either reading public facts from it or carrying a copy of an attestation on a test network, never deriving our trust from it.
anchoring.why: Resolves the live contradiction between 'nothing is anchored to a blockchain' (homepage, /coliseum, /evidence, /live-ledger) and 'XRPL attestation' (/xrpl-attest, /distribution-integrity, /financial-axes). Both are true of DIFFERENT things: our own trust root is the signature chain; XRPL is a data source we read (mainnet) and a carrier we test on (devnet).
anchoring.short_form: Our anchor is a signature, not a chain. We read ledgers; we do not anchor to them.

doctrine_verbatim: We measure, we sign, we re-attest.
We do NOT certify, accredit, enforce, endorse, or tokenize.
Not a certification body, not a notified body.
No money from anything we rank.
Verification is free forever; a grade is never sold.
boundary.evidence: GET /api/gspc -> limitations[8]: 'CSOAI is a measurement body, not a certification or accreditation body, and not a notified body.'; note: 'Measurement, not certification.'
negation_forms_that_must_pass: we do not certify, accredit or approve anything
It attests training, not conformity — we certify nothing
we measure, we do not certify
nothing here is a conformity assessment
boundary.gate_note: The negation forms above are LOAD-BEARING TEST CASES, verified present on the live site 2026-08-26. 'we certify nothing' is a negation-by-object and is the form most likely to be mis-flagged. A gate that fails any of these is over-broad and will be disabled — which is how this class of gate died before.

alignment_audit_2026_08_26.note: Record audit: public board locked at 14 (5477ef62 + ebec824e); '22 at 2bdbac34' NOT corroborated; card index frozen at verifiable floor 150 (BOARD-RULING.md corrected ruling, UNMEASURED-before-measured for the 185); public count = live sentence only; 22 = internal map with WARNING.
alignment_audit_2026_08_26.correction_2026_08_26_pm: CORRECTED, with checkable evidence. This audit recorded "'22 at 2bdbac34' NOT corroborated (commit nonexistent)". The commit EXISTS. It was searched for in councilof-ai, but ADR-001 names it in a different repo. Verified via the GitHub API: CSOAI-ORG/csoai-static-deploy2 commit 2bdbac34986333f6de992fcd76cb08aa3e19d1cf, authored by Nicholas Templeman on 2026-08-24T12:30:30Z, subject 'canon: 22 measurement axes (14/14 GSPC incl. jail measured + 8 financial) — owner ruling 2026-08-24'. The jail measurement commit ADR-001 cites, 70451d3ddf72211b811dd5670281142fa28e0314 (2026-08-21), exists in the same repo. The audit's other findings stand; only the corroboration finding is corrected. The failure mode is worth recording on its own: a citation was judged nonexistent because it was looked for in the wrong repository, and a settled owner ruling was nearly re-derived from that absence.
alignment_audit_2026_08_26.reconciliation: 5477ef62 and ebec824e (both 2026-08-26 00:xx) lock the PUBLIC board at 14 and warn against INVENTING 22. They are not in conflict with the 2026-08-24 ruling: they forbid publishing the number without the signed data behind it, which is precisely the condition ADR-001 records as blocking the sweep. The sweep of 2026-08-26 supplied that data and re-signed the payload, so the guardrail's condition is satisfied rather than overridden. Nothing was typed: every count is derived from the axis array.
